Star Legend Review

Review of Star Legend

The 1992-built (as "Royal Viking Queen") and acquired in 2015 from Seabourn (as "Seabourn Legend"), Star Legend is the third and final of the three identical superyachts in the Windstar fleet, together with Star Pride (Seabourn Pride) and Star Breeze (Seabourn Spirit).

The vessel (IMO number 9008598) is currently Bahamas-flagged (MMSI 311085000) and registered in Nassau.

History - construction and ownership

Windstar Cruises is a luxury travel brand operating a fleet of small-sized ships (mega-yachts) with capacity up to 340 passengers. The company calls at 150 ports across the Caribbean, Central America, the South Pacific, Asia, and Europe. Windstar is currently a subsidiary of Xanterra Parks and Resorts (the USA's largest national and state park concession management company).

The 340-passenger ship Star Legend was constructed in Bremerhaven Germany (by Schichau-Seebeckwerft) and inaugurated in February 1992 by Kloster Cruise. She was originally named "Royal Viking Queen" and operated by Royal Viking Line (founded in 1972, defunct since 1998). In 1995, the vessel was renamed "Queen Odyssey" and operated by Royal Cruise Line (1995-1996), before being sold to Seabourn Cruises and renamed "Seabourn Legend." In April 2015, the ship left Seabourn and joined Windstar’s fleet in May as "Star Legend."

An interesting fact is that Seabourn Legend was featured in the film "Speed 2: Cruise Control" (1997, starring Sandra Bullock, Jason Patric, and Willem Dafoe). In the movie, Alex Shaw (Jason Patric) and Annie Porter (Sandra Bullock) are trapped onboard after the ship’s navigation systems are reprogrammed by a hacker (Willem Dafoe), setting the vessel on a collision course with a supertanker.

Decks and Cabins

Star Legend staterooms (156 total, in 13 grades) are all outside and exclusively suite accommodations, with the lowest category being Porthole Suite (10 cabins). All suites feature modern amenities, including fully stocked minibars, Wi-Fi Internet, smart HDTVs (infotainment system), spacious wardrobes with electronic safes, direct-dial phones, and large bathrooms (double-sink vanity, bathtub, shower, WC-toilet, L'Occitane bath products), as well as premium bedding (high-quality pillows and linens), fresh fruit, and flowers.

The largest accommodations are the 3-Bedroom Grand Owner's Suites (1375 ft² / 128 m²), which include private outdoor terraces.

The ship has 8 decks, of which 6 are passenger-accessible and 4 with cabins.

Shipboard dining options - Food and Drinks

A major advantage of Star Legend is the wide variety of dining options for a ship of her size. Guests can choose from several inclusive venues, including AmphorA Restaurant, Yacht Club, and Sky Bar & Grill. Windstar guests often enjoy dressing up—there are 2 formal nights on weeklong cruises and 3 on 14-day voyages. On these evenings, many men wear tuxedos, while women opt for cocktail dresses or evening gowns. Other nights follow a casually elegant dress code (jackets for men, ties optional; stylish attire for women) or casual dress (no jacket for men; sundresses or slacks for women). Guests preferring a relaxed atmosphere can dine at the Veranda Cafe.

Follows the complete list of Star Legend restaurants and food bars.

  • AmphorA Restaurant (main dining room with open seating; offers a daily-changing 5-course gourmet dinner menu; the executive chef sources fresh ingredients from local markets in ports of call)
  • Candles Cafe & Veranda (a smaller dining venue offering buffet-style breakfast and lunch, plus a la carte service; indoor "Candles Cafe" features floor-to-ceiling windows, while the outdoor "Veranda" transforms into "Candles Grill," an alfresco steakhouse in the evenings)
  • Star Bar (serving the open-air top deck area)
  • Basil+Bamboo (deck 6 aft portside, complimentary specialty restaurant serving Mediterranean-Asian fusion cuisine)
  • Star Grill by Steven Raichlen (deck 8 midship, an alfresco venue serving complimentary BBQ cuisine)

In 2025 (on Star Breeze), Windstar introduced the specialty restaurant Basil+Bamboo fleetwide, replacing Cuadro 44 by Anthony Sasso (Iberian cuisine). The new venue is complimentary and serves Mediterranean-Asian fusion dishes. The menu includes items such as miso black cod with pea puree, jamon Iberico de Bellota, pickled wood ear mushrooms, free-range chicken with artichokes and yuzu kosho, crispy Brussels sprouts in Korean honey-soy sauce, and gourmet desserts like Citrus Olive Oil Cake and Chocolate Caramel Cremeux, paired with ginger-cinnamon hibiscus ice cream and sake caviar.

Also complimentary is Windstar's 24-hour room service. During dinner hours, AmphorA Restaurant’s full menu is also available for in-suite dining.

Shipboard entertainment options - Fun and Sport

Onboard activities on Star Legend are relatively limited and include market tours, enrichment programs, and performances by local musicians. Public areas include a casino, library, computer center, WindSpa, fitness center, swimming pool, and three whirlpools.

Follows the complete list of Star Legend lounges, clubs, and other entertainment venues for guests of all ages.

  • The Marina (retractable watersports platform for water skiing, windsurfing, snorkeling, and kayaking; equipment includes water rafts, wakeboards, paddleboards, and a water trampoline; a steel enclosure can be used as a sea pool)
  • A whirlpool (with a sunbathing area and loungers)
  • Card Room (bridge and board games), Library, Screening Room
  • Computer Center (Internet access with per-minute rates)
  • Lounge (main show lounge for live evening entertainment)
  • The Boutique Shop (now Signature Shop) offering duty-free luxury fashion and accessories
  • The Casino (formerly located aft on deck 6, replaced by Cuadro 44 restaurant)
  • Compass Rose (main bar lounge with grand piano)
  • The Wellness Centre (WindSpa, beauty salon, gym; includes treatment rooms, saunas, and steam rooms)
  • The Fitness Center (with floor-to-ceiling windows; equipped with free weights, treadmills, and elliptical machines; offers complimentary classes), Courtyard
  • Pool Area (with one rectangular pool, two whirlpools on platforms, and a third whirlpool at the bow; includes sunbathing and shaded areas)
  • The Yacht Club (Constellation Lounge with floor-to-ceiling windows offering 270-degree views)
  • The Sun Deck (with padded luxury loungers and deckchairs)

Itineraries

Star Legend's itinerary program focuses on Mediterranean cruises, with departures mainly from ports in France, Italy, and Spain. In Northern Europe, the ship operates Baltic Sea and Norwegian Fjords itineraries, as well as voyages to Iceland, departing from Denmark and the UK.

In November 2016, Windstar announced a return to Asia (for the first time in three years), deploying Star Legend in the region for the winter 2017-2018 season. The program included itineraries from Thailand, Malaysia, and Singapore to destinations in South Korea and Japan.

In 2018, Windstar homeported Star Legend in Vancouver BC Canada, operating three distinct itineraries (May through August), including 11- and 12-day Alaska voyages from Vancouver to Seward, 14-day Seward-to-Vancouver cruises, and two 12-day roundtrips from Vancouver. The Alaska program also included pre- and post-cruise land tour packages.

In 2023, Star Legend completed Windstar's longest voyage—the "Star Collector - Grand European Bucket List Adventure." The 79-night itinerary (ship's Wiki section) departed Stockholm on July 25 and ended in Istanbul on October 12. Prices started from USD 40,000/EUR 34,035 per person with double occupancy.

In October 2023, Star Legend's inaugural Middle East season (November 2023 through April 2024, based on homeporting in Dubai UAE) was canceled and rescheduled for the 2024-2025 season (November through April).

Star Legend Wiki

Star Legend was operated by Seabourn as "Seabourn Legend." The vessel was originally built for and owned by Kloster Cruise and operated by its subsidiary Royal Viking Line under the name "Royal Viking Queen." In 1995, Kloster Cruise transferred her to another subsidiary, Royal Cruise Line, and renamed her "Queen Odyssey." In 1996, the ship was purchased by Seabourn Cruises. Seabourn Legend entered Windstar's fleet in April 2015 (in active service since May 2015).

Star Legend's godmother is Gloria Bohan (CEO of "Omega World Travel"—a corporate travel management company specializing in business meetings and events at sea). The christening ceremony took place on May 25, 2015, in Civitavecchia-Rome. The ship's 3-week drydock refit and refurbishment in 2015 was carried out in Genoa Italy. The USD 8.5 million renovation included stern-to-bow upgrades, expansion of the Veranda Cafe and Star Deck, and the addition of Windstar's Yacht Club, an infinity (resistance) pool, and a whirlpool.

A fun fact is that Seabourn Legend was featured as the background ship in the movie "Speed 2." Annie Porter (Sandra Bullock) and her boyfriend Alex Shaw (Jason Patric), an LAPD police officer, are trapped onboard while the ship’s navigation systems are hacked by the villain John Geiger (Willem Dafoe), setting the vessel on a collision course with a large tanker.

During the ship's week-long drydock refurbishment in December 2017 (in Singapore), the Transas A-Suite e-navigation system and Navi-Radar 4000 (by DP Marine, with integrated JRC sensors) were installed. The system includes two radars (X-band and S-band), dual ECDIS (Electronic Chart Display and Information System), K-Nav ECDIS (route planning station by Kongsberg Maritime), and PilotStar NX autopilot (by Anschutz). All bridge consoles and the ship’s antenna systems were also upgraded.

Grand Voyage 2023

In mid-August 2021, Windstar opened bookings for its longest voyage to date—the 79-day "Grand European Bucket List Adventure," scheduled for summer 2023.

WINDSTAR cruise ship reconstructions 2019-2020-2021 drydock refurbishments review

On November 15, 2018, Windstar announced the company's "Star Plus Initiative" - drydock refit and refurbishment program budgeted USD 250 million. The project was partially financed through an Export Credit facility guaranteed by SACE Italy (financial and insurance products and services). The "Star Plus" drydocking project includes enlarging (stretching) and engine upgrades for the fleet's three Star-Class vessels (in brackets - completion dates) - Star Breeze (February 20, 2020), Star Legend (July 2, 2020) and Star Pride (November 20, 2020).

Windstar's "Star Plus" project increased the fleet's capacity by 24%. The project (completed in October 2021) resulted in bigger capacity (254 to 320 passengers, 140 to 190 crew), increased GT tonnage/volume (9975 to 12995 tons), increased length (134 to 159 m), more staterooms (106 to 156), adding new venues and public spaces, machinery upgrades (new Wartsila marine diesel engines). The project was scheduled for the period October 2019 through November 2020, at Fincantieri's shipyards in Palermo (Sicily Island, Italy) and Trieste (Italy).

The drydock lengthening included cutting each vessel in two and installing a new (prefabricated) midship section with length 25 m (83 ft). The vessel's LOA length was increased from 134 m (439 ft) to 159 m (522). The midship section has an additional elevator. These sections were built (pre-fabricated and assembled) in Trieste, and then barged to Palermo to be inserted into the vessels.

 

Following the drydocks, each ship now has 2 new dining venues (Cuadro 44 by Anthony Sasso, Star Grill by Steven Raichlen), new / expanded retail shopping space (Signature Shop), enlarged Gym (Fitness Center with Motion Studio for classes), expanded wellness complex (WindSpa by Steiner), new bar lounge (deck 5), larger sundeck and swimming pool (deck 7), new tender loading area (deck 3 midship), two new tender boats (90-seat each), new whirlpool and enlarged swimming pool (on deck 8), expanded and upgraded staff-crew areas and crew cabins. The two new dining venues are a specialty restaurant (Cuadro 44, aft-portside on deck 6, the former Casino area) and a casual outdoor BBQ restaurant (Star Grill, adjacent to Star Bar on deck 8).

The powerplants were upgraded from 4x Bergen diesel engines (model B33:45, combined power output 7,3 MW) to 4x Wartsila engines (model Wartsila 46F, combined output 5 MW) running on the cleaner ULSD (ultra-low sulfur diesel) fuel.

Each boat received 50 new cabins (to a total of 156), which (based on the total investment) means shipbuilding cost per berth USD 267,000. Among the new cabins are two Midship Owner Suites and two enlarged Forward Grand Owner Suites - all located on Deck 6. All existing staterooms were completely refurbished, including bathrooms, balconies, sliding doors, furniture, equipment. The new public spaces and staterooms were designed by the NYC-based "The Johnson Studio at Cooper Carry".
